summary: Unexplained private VPC egress fee on invoice attributed to hosted fallback window
description: Issue summary: Customer BrightDocs reports an unexpected egress charge on their monthly invoice (~$1,764) for a private VPC deployment where they claim no public egress occurred. Impact: Billing surprise and potential contract dispute; customer requests urgent correction and explanation. Environment: private deployment (VPC), prod, region us-east, reserved hours active. Observed behavior: invoice line item 'VPC EGRESS SURCHARGE' appears for 2026-02-26 03:00-04:00 UTC coincident with a hosted fallback event. Expected behavior: Private deployment traffic should not incur hosted egress charges; fallback to hosted should bill hosted compute (tokens) but not private VPC egress for customer's private connector.
impact: Customer-facing invoice overcharge; escalated to finance and account team. Potential churn risk if unresolved within billing cycle.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer triggered a model request against private deployment endpoint behind VPC connector.
2) At 2026-02-26 02:58 UTC, internal autoscaler briefly removed private pool nodes for maintenance and traffic routed to hosted fallback pool.
3) Hosted fallback served requests for ~6 minutes (02:59-03:05 UTC) and then returned to private pool.
4) Customer received a VPC EGRESS line on monthly invoice for that time window despite the private network showing no egress bytes in their VPC flow logs.
investigation_notes: Checked postback logs: postback batch 2026-02-26T03:02:00Z recorded tags: tenant_id=brightdocs, env=private, connector_id=vpc-123, meter_tags=[hosted_fallback:true, egress:true] (unexpected)

Querying metering pipeline: found tag-normalizer job failed to find connector mapping for connector_id=vpc-123 during a transient schema migration (schema v2->v3) and defaulted to legacy tag set which marks fallback requests with 'egress:true' for retrospective billing classification.
Cross-referenced VPC flow logs (customer-provided): zero bytes to 0.0.0.0/0 for the window 02:50-03:10 UTC; only internal AWS ENI traffic observed.

Console metrics: hosted pool served ~1.4k tokens during fallback window. Postback attribution shows two line items created: hosted compute tokens (correct) and VPC EGRESS (incorrectly added by tag normalization).

Related PRs: meter pipeline PR 387 changed default behaviour for missing connector mappings and introduced a fallback flag that was intended to be false for private connectors; issue reproduced in staging when connector mapping service responded with 500.

resolution: Workaround: Manual invoice credit of $1,764 applied to BrightDocs' account (see ledger note). Mitigation: Hotfix merged to tag-normalizer to treat missing connector mappings as 'private:false, egress:false' for fallback classification; hotfix deployed to staging and validated against synthetic connectors. Planned prod deployment on 2026-03-14 during low-traffic window with monitoring alert. Follow-up actions: run a 7-day backfill audit to find any other invoices with misattributed 'VPC EGRESS' lines; finance to issue retroactive credits if found; postmortem and a ticket to add circuit-breaker to mapping service so failures default to safe billing classification. Customer requested final postmortem and confirmation of credits issued before case closure.
